survey: A carved jack-o'-lantern seen in a slight three-quarter view, sitting on a wooden plank table. The body is a squat, ribbed pumpkin, and its vertical ribs meet at the top around a short green stem. The stem grows out of the top centre and bends slightly forward. The face faces the camera: two triangular eyes and a wide zigzag mouth are cut through the rind. Each opening shows a bevelled cut wall and a warm yellow glow inside, which is what a candle or light in a hollow pumpkin would give. The bottom of the pumpkin touches the table and casts a contact shadow to the right and behind, so it rests on the surface and does not float. The left eye looks narrower than the right because it turns away from the camera, which matches the view angle. There is no visible lid cut around the stem. That is a common simplification, since pumpkins can be carved from the bottom, and not a construction fault. Every part attaches where it should and the object could work as a lantern.
